title: P22 x P19 handoff plasticity: hand RL the 129-claude model with every Peri-LN-normalized branch output projection (proj, fc2) halved and its output-LN eps quartered, the same function with a 2x larger RL step on those matrices (4,800,000 params)
description: P22 x P19 follow-up (Peri-LN scale invariance, LR-floor plasticity): after pretraining, multiply every block's proj and fc2 by 0.5 and the eps of the LayerNorm that normalizes that branch output by 0.25, which leaves the handed-off function exactly unchanged but doubles the angle each frozen-RL AdamW step turns those 12 matrices. 129-claude's floor 0.1 -> 0.3 keep (+15) came with a worse round-1 harvest (-75 targets) but a faster r1->r4 climb, so its surviving explanation is a more plastic handoff; this isolates plasticity from sampler quality: same round-1 start as 129, more RL movement where the Peri-LN output norms make weight scale matter only for step size.
hypothesis: With Peri-LN, proj and fc2 feed a LayerNorm directly, so their norm does not affect the function, only the effective step: the frozen RL's AdamW moves each coordinate by ~lr regardless of weight size, so the angular change per step scales as 1/||W||. 129's evidence (higher floor: worse start, faster expert-iteration climb, more >=7 solves; 131's SWA: better start, same RL total, fewer >=7 solves; 130's constant LR: fastest climb but broken start) says the fixed RL benefits from a handoff that can still move, and that sampler quality at handoff is not the lever. Halving these norms keeps 129's exact sampler for round 1 and doubles RL plasticity in the branch writes, so rounds 2-4 should adapt faster to the >=7 proofs they harvest. Failure modes: (a) RL is already plastic enough and the extra rotation is noise that erodes pretrained skill (post-RL greedy falls, parse failures rise in rounds 2-4); (b) Adam's norm growth (orthogonal updates grow ||W||) quickly restores the old effective step, making this a near no-op.
expected_delta: -45 to +35 theorems at >=7 (central +3); pretraining identical to 129 in distribution: 4,100-4,300 steps (129: 4238/4137/4233), final train loss ~0.053-0.055, final val loss 0.073-0.083; held-out greedy at handoff 0.950-0.970 (129: 0.9625/0.9635/0.955) because the function is unchanged; round-1 targets solved within +-40 of 129's 647/610/684 per seed; r1->r4 RL-solved growth above 129's +478 mean if the mechanism holds; branch_out_rms 0.004-0.03 per matrix; total time within 100 s of 129's 1727 s max

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input) and hybrid attention heads, ALiBi on 4 heads and no positional signal on the other 4 (P34 x P32); architecture unchanged from 129-claude except the handoff rescale below, which changes parameter values and two LayerNorm eps but not the function
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107); eps 1e-5 everywhere during pretraining; at handoff the 12 branch-output LayerNorms (ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out) get eps 1e-5 * 0.5^2 = 2.5e-6, which RL and eval keep (ln1, ln2, ln_f stay 1e-5)
arch.change: handoff-only (HANDOFF_SCALE 0.5): after the last pretraining step, every block's proj (attention output) and fc2 (MLP output) weight, and bias if the fork's Linear has one, is multiplied by 0.5 and the LayerNorm that normalizes that branch output gets eps * 0.25. LN(c z; c^2 eps) = LN(z; eps) exactly, so the handed-off model computes the same function as 129's endpoint (CPU float64 check on a Peri-LN MLP branch with small weights: max abs diff 0.0; without the eps change 5.4e-3). Pretraining itself is byte-identical to 129-claude
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 129-claude: 4,800,000 (vocab 107); rescale changes values, not count; slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py, replace blocks with PeriLNBlock, load state, and set every block's ln_attn_out.eps and ln_mlp_out.eps to 2.5e-6 (eps is not in state_dict; with the default 1e-5 the reloaded model differs slightly from the handed-off one). The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval, so it sees the rescaled eps
arch.kv_cache: unchanged from 129-claude (caches[0] holds key positions; slope-0 heads get a zero bias plus the -inf mask)

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129-claude: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak. Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 follows the same factor, and so does its per-step decoupled decay lr * MUON_WD

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged from 129-claude); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1 applied as p *= 1 - muon_lr * 0.1 on all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1. With output LayerNorms, the scale of proj/fc2 does not reach the residual stream; it only sets their effective step size (angular step ~ update / norm)
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW (lr 3e-4, wd 0.1, betas 0.9/0.95, clip 1.0). NEW: proj and fc2 are handed off at half their trained norm (function unchanged via the eps rescale), so each RL AdamW step (per-coordinate size set by lr, not by the weight) rotates those 12 matrices by ~2x the angle it would under 129; their gradients are 2x larger, which Adam normalizes out. qkv, fc1, head, embeddings and all LayerNorm parameters are untouched
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1

handoff_rescale.matrices: blocks[0..5].proj and blocks[0..5].fc2 (weights; biases too if present), 12 matrices, 6 x (65,536 + 262,144) = 1,966,080 weights
handoff_rescale.when: once, after the final pretraining step and the last curve point, before model.eval() and return; inside torch.no_grad()
handoff_rescale.diagnostic: stats.branch_out_rms: element RMS of the 12 weights before rescaling (proj x6 then fc2 x6)
handoff_rescale.not_changed: pretraining loss, curve, steps, val_loss and every pretraining hyperparameter are those of 129-claude
